newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-FLYERS BEAT RANGERS TO EARN STANLEY CUP FINALS BERTH. [CORRECTED 23:55 GMT]
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-FLYERS BEAT RANGERS TO EARN STANLEY CUP FINALS BERTH. [CORRECTED 23:55 GMT]

text.p: Rod Brind'Amour scored twice, including the go-ahead goal, to return the Philadelphia Flyers to the Stanley Cup Finals for the first time in a decade with a 4-2 victory over the New York Rangers Sunday.

Eric Lindros and John LeClair added power-play tallies for the Flyers, who won the last three games to take the best-of-seven Eastern Conference finals 4-1. Philadelphia will play the winner of the Western Conference series between Colorado and Detroit in the Stanley Cup Finals.

Ron Hextall, who won the Conn Smythe Trophy during the Flyers' last trip to the Stanley Cup Finals in 1987, turned aside 17 shots. He won the final three contests after replacing Garth Snow in the second period of Game 2.
Brind'Amour capped a wild first period when he grabbed a loose puck in the low slot, faked Mike Richter and slid a backhander between the goaltender's pads for his ninth playoff goal.

Philadelphia limited the Rangers to two shots in the second period, then dodged a bullet early in the third when New York's Wayne Gretzky came out from behind the net and flicked a backhander off the right goalpost.

Brind'Amour got his fourth goal of the series at 6:43 to provide the Flyers with insurance. He won a faceoff deep in the Rangers' zone and fed the puck back to Chris Therien at the left point. Richter got his left pad on Therien's slap shot, but Brind'Amour chipped in the rebound to make it 4-2.

Gretzky missed another chance from close range with 4:20 remaining and Philadelphia's CoreStates Centre erupted as the clock ran out and the Flyers moved on to the Stanley Cup Finals for the seventh (corrects from fifth) time in the franchise's 29-year history.
Only the Montreal Canadiens, Boston Bruins and Edmonton Oilers have made more appearances in the Finals over that stretch.

Philadelphia got the first goal in all five games of the series. New York's Adam Graves was penalised for tripping 4:48 into the game and Lindros made it 1-0 just 20 seconds later, backhanding his own rebound past Richter for his fifth goal in three games.

The Rangers got back-to-back power-play goals in a 26-second span to grab a 2-1 lead. They had a 5-on-3 advantage when Alexander Karpovtsev one-timed a wrist shot into the top left corner of the net from the left circle. Karpovtsev missed the previous two games after returning to Russia following the death of his mother.

New York was still on the power play when Karpovtsev's shot caromed off the end boards onto the stick of Esa Tikkanen, who tucked the puck past Hextall for his ninth playoff goal with 7:04 to go in the period.
But the Flyers, who were 6-for-21 on the power play in the series, evened it up with the man advantage just under three minutes later.

Rangers defenceman Jeff Beukeboom was serving a cross-checking penalty when Eric Desjardins broke down the right wing and threw a pass in front just before going behind the net. LeClair shook free from Bruce Driver at the top of the crease and banged the puck through Richter's pads for his seventh playoff goal.
Richter, a native of suburban Philadelphia, finished with 25 saves but surrendered 19 goals in the series after allowing just 14 in the first two rounds combined.
